title: What lies behind about fifteen minutes?
description: A speech bubble reads I take about 15 minutes to cycle from school to home. The board shows many different days of riding, then one number that stands for all of them. Keeko doubts that the statement is only about one ride.
teaching_notes: One idea: a statistical statement gives one number for many values that vary. Watch for students who think the statement describes a single trip.

source: Read the statement 'I take about 15 minutes to cycle from sc
video_script.why: The child hears such claims every day but has not asked what data stands behind the number.
video_script.substitution: The statement is true for many days of riding, not for one trip.
video_script.anchor: A speech bubble with the book's statement beside a cyclist and a row of calendar days
video_script.wrong_answer: the statement is about one ride, the ride home today
video_script.wrong_move: reads the statement as describing a single trip
video_script.payoff_line: Fifteen minutes sums up many ride times that vary from day to day

final_answer.value: It is a statistical statement because 15 minutes sums up many ride times that vary from day to day
final_answer.spoken: it is a statistical statement because fifteen minutes sums up many ride times that vary from day to day

maths_rules: the statement says about 15 minutes, as in the book
the rider has cycled home on many days and the times differ a little from day to day
one number, 15, stands for all those days
a claim or summary in numbers is a statistical statement
video_script.design: A speech bubble, then many days of riding with slightly different clocks, then one number for them all. Only the book's words are used; no ride time is invented.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a line from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A child says, I take about fifteen minutes to cycle from school to home.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The number fifteen sounds so sure.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>What must the child have done to be able to say it?

beats.on_screen: the label statistical statement appears under the bubble: a claim or summary expressed in numbers

marks.g2: the label statistical statement appears under the bubble

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>A claim or summary that is given in numbers
<bookmark mark='g2'/>is called a statistical statement.

beats.on_screen: Given: the statement I take about 15 minutes to cycle from school to home

marks.given: the statement is written at the top of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the statement says it takes about fifteen minutes to cycle from school to home.

beats.on_screen: To find: why it is a statistical statement, and what data is behind it

marks.find: the words data and behind are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find why it is a statistical statement, and what data is behind it.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the rider has cycled home on many days, so there are many ride times

marks.s1: a row of calendar days appears
marks.s2: a clock lights up on each day

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, the rider has cycled home on many days.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>There are many ride times, and they are the data behind the statement.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the clocks differ a little from day to day, and the word about tells us this

marks.d1: the clocks show slightly different times
marks.d2: the word about is circled in the statement

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, some days take a little less time and some days a little more.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>The word about is there because the ride times differ.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: one number, 15, is used for all the days

marks.c1: all the clocks slide into the number 15

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, one number is used for all those days.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>That number is fifteen, and it makes the claim a statistical statement.

beats.on_screen: Answer: it is a statistical statement because 15 minutes sums up many ride times that vary from day to day
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Fifteen minutes sums up many ride times that vary from day to day.
It is a statistical statement, and the data is those ride times.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's thought bubble circles one clock on the calendar; the other clocks then light up and the circle is struck through

marks.doubt: the bubble with one circled clock appears
marks.fix: the other clocks on the calendar light up

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the statement is about one ride, the ride home today.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the child never said today, and never named one trip.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>The word about tells us the rides were not all the same.
